fields.title: From Users to Resources
fields.keyTakeaway: As audience grows, accumulated data grows faster than load, and the main value of the calculation is to spot thresholds that would otherwise be crossed unnoticed.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: Planning for 5x growth in a year. What grows 5x, and what grows differently?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: Growth plans not translated into resources lead to infrastructure hitting a ceiling mid-year. The translation takes an hour and is done once.
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/text: **Grow proportionally to users:** requests per second, event volume, traffic, cost of requests to external providers.
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: **Grow faster:** accumulated data volume — it grows like an integral, meaning it increases regardless with a steady influx. If audience doubles, accumulation speeds up twofold, and the volume in two years will grow 4x relative to the first year.
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: **Grow slower or don't grow:** catalog size, number of partners, team cost, fixed parts of infrastructure.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: **Grow in steps:** anything that has thresholds. The database handles load up to a limit, then requires sharding. The number of instances hits the connection limit.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: A practical planning table: metric, current value, growth factor, value in a year, whether there is a threshold along the way.
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: The "has threshold" column is the most valuable. That is where you discover that with 5x growth, we will cross a boundary twice that requires architectural work.
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/text: Planning for 3x growth in a year:
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: Three thresholds instead of the expected one. We knew about the database size—that is work from the `DS2-G-B` gate. The connection limit and analytics tier were discovered precisely through this exercise, and both would have been crossed unnoticed, resulting in outages.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: An hour of work added two items to the roadmap half a year before they would have become incidents.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: Linear extrapolation is bad when the product profile changes: a new audience segment may behave differently. The rough estimate is needed as a signal, not as a forecast.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: As audience grows, accumulated data grows faster than load, and the main value of the calculation is to spot thresholds that would otherwise be crossed unnoticed.
